Method of Attack: Encrypts victim's files and demands ransom for decryptor
Skips encryption of files in specific system and user folders (bypass list)
Prioritizes encryption of certain folders related to bitcoin, Microsoft Office, Steam, and others
Scrambles file names and extensions of encrypted files
Changes Windows desktop background to mimic Cerber ransomware
Blocks execution on virtual machines by detecting VM-related processes, files, and named pipes
Partially encrypts files starting at offset 0x708 bytes
Ransom note directs victims to contact via ToxChat messaging app
Impacted Systems: Microsoft Office suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint, OneNote, Outlook)
Indicators of Compromise: Bypassed folders list (e.g., $getcurrent, $recycle.bin, program files, appdata folders, windows folders)
Priority folders list (e.g., bitcoin, microsoft\excel, office, steam, autodesk)
VM detection processes and files (e.g., prl_cc.exe, vboxservice.exe, vmtoolsd.exe, vmwareuser.exe, VBoxMiniRdrDN, VBoxGuest.sys)
Partial file encryption starting at 0x708 bytes
Ransom note referencing ToxChat messaging app
Desktop background image similar to Cerber ransomware
